politics.text: Spanish adventurers led by Hernán Cortés are received by Aztec emperor Moctezuma II at his capital, Tenochtitlan.
politics.context: The meeting took place in November. Within two years Cortés had destroyed the Aztec empire.

politics.text: Charles of Habsburg, king of Spain, is elected Holy Roman Emperor as Charles V, beating King Francis I of France to the crown.
politics.context: He was elected in June, after a costly campaign of bribes to the electors.

society.text: The Swiss priest Huldrych Zwingli begins preaching straight from the Gospels in Zurich, breaking with church custom.
society.context: He started at the Grossmünster on New Year's Day, launching the Swiss Reformation.

society.text: Hernán Cortés founds the town of Veracruz on the Mexican coast, the first Spanish settlement on the mainland of New Spain.
society.context: He founded it in April, then scuttled his ships to stop his men from turning back.

technology.text: Five ships under the Portuguese captain Ferdinand Magellan leave Seville on the first voyage to sail around the world.
technology.context: Magellan died on the way. The Spanish navigator Elcano brought the survivors home in 1522.

arts_culture.text: The Italian painter and inventor Leonardo da Vinci dies at Amboise, in France, as a guest of King Francis I.
King Francis I of France orders the building of the Château de Chambord, a vast hunting lodge in the Loire valley.

politics.text: Hernán Cortés and his native allies capture Tenochtitlan after a long siege, ending the Aztec empire.
politics.context: The city fell in August. It became the site of Mexico City.

politics.text: The Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent captures the fortress of Belgrade, opening the way into Hungary.
politics.context: Belgrade fell in August.

society.text: The German monk Martin Luther refuses to retract his writings before Emperor Charles V and is declared an outlaw.
society.context: He appeared at the Diet of Worms in April. The Edict of Worms followed in May.

technology.text: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish-sponsored fleet reaches the Philippines, named later for King Philip of Spain.
technology.context: Magellan reached the islands in March and was killed there a month later.

arts_culture.text: The Franco-Flemish composer Josquin des Prez, the most admired musician of his age, dies in Condé-sur-l'Escaut.
arts_culture.context: He died in August, in what is now northern France.

politics.text: Portuguese sailors blown off course land on Tanegashima, in Japan, and introduce the first firearms to the country.
politics.context: Japanese smiths copied the guns within a few years.

society.text: King Henry VIII of England marries his sixth and last wife, Catherine Parr, at Hampton Court.
society.context: The wedding was in July. She outlived him.

technology.text: The Polish astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus publishes his theory that the Earth orbits the Sun, as he lies dying.
technology.context: The book was De revolutionibus. He is said to have seen a printed copy on his deathbed.

technology.text: The Flemish anatomist Andreas Vesalius publishes On the Fabric of the Human Body, a landmark of anatomy, in Basel.
technology.context: The book was based on his own dissections and corrected centuries-old errors.

arts_culture.text: The German painter Hans Holbein the Younger, court artist to King Henry VIII, dies in London.
arts_culture.context: He probably died of plague in the autumn.

politics.text: The Spanish execute Túpac Amaru, the last ruler of the Inca state at Vilcabamba, in the main square of Cusco.
politics.context: He was captured in the summer and executed in September.

society.text: Catholic mobs in Paris murder thousands of Protestant Huguenots in the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre.
society.context: The killings began in August and spread to other French cities.

technology.text: The Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe observes a brilliant new star in the constellation Cassiopeia.
technology.context: He saw it in November. It was a supernova, and it challenged the idea of an unchanging sky.

arts_culture.text: The Portuguese poet Luís de Camões publishes The Lusiads, an epic poem about Vasco da Gama's voyage to India.

politics.text: The Japanese warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi sends a huge army across the sea to invade Korea, beginning the Imjin War.
politics.context: The first landings were in April.

society.text: Plague closes London's theatres, leaving actors and playwrights without work.
society.context: The theatres were shut for much of the year and the next.

technology.text: The Korean admiral Yi Sun-sin destroys a Japanese fleet with his armoured turtle ships at the Battle of Hansando.
technology.context: It was fought in August.

arts_culture.text: A pamphlet by the writer Robert Greene attacks an "upstart crow", the first known mention of William Shakespeare as a London playwright.
arts_culture.context: Greene wrote it as he lay dying, in the early autumn.

politics.text: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats rival warlords at the Battle of Sekigahara, in Japan, clearing his path to become shogun.
politics.context: It was fought in October. He took the title of shogun three years later.

society.text: Queen Elizabeth I grants a royal charter to the English East India Company, a trading firm that will come to rule much of India.
society.context: The charter was granted on the last day of the year.

society.text: The Italian philosopher Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome for heresy.
society.context: He was executed in February.

technology.text: The English physician William Gilbert publishes De Magnete, arguing that the Earth itself is a giant magnet.
technology.context: Gilbert was physician to Queen Elizabeth I.

arts_culture.text: The Italian composer Jacopo Peri's Euridice, the earliest opera that survives, is first performed in Florence.
arts_culture.context: It was staged in October, at the wedding of Maria de' Medici and King Henry IV of France.

politics.text: Akbar, the great Mughal emperor of India, dies at Agra, and his son Jahangir takes the throne.
politics.context: Akbar died in October after a reign of nearly fifty years.

society.text: English Catholics led by Guy Fawkes are foiled in a plot to blow up King James I and Parliament in London.
society.context: Fawkes was caught guarding barrels of gunpowder beneath the Parliament building in November.

technology.text: The printer Johann Carolus begins publishing a weekly newsletter in Strasbourg, often called the first newspaper.
technology.context: The weekly was called Relation. It is usually counted as the first printed newspaper.

arts_culture.text: The Spanish writer Miguel de Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quixote, a novel about a deluded knight.
arts_culture.context: The first part appeared in Madrid in January.

politics.text: Japan's Satsuma clan invades the Ryukyu Kingdom and takes its king prisoner.
politics.context: The invasion began in the spring. The kingdom, on Okinawa, became a vassal of Satsuma.

politics.text: Spain and the Dutch Republic agree the Twelve Years' Truce, pausing a long war.
politics.context: The truce was signed in April.

society.text: The English explorer Henry Hudson, sailing for the Dutch, enters the North American river that will bear his name.
society.context: He sailed up the river in September, looking for a route to Asia.

technology.text: The Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei builds a telescope in Venice and turns it on the Moon, seeing mountains and craters.
technology.context: He built it in August and began studying the Moon in the autumn.

arts_culture.text: William Shakespeare's Sonnets are published in London, probably without his permission.
arts_culture.context: The book contained 154 sonnets and was printed by Thomas Thorpe.

politics.text: King Henry IV of France is stabbed to death in his carriage in Paris by a Catholic fanatic, François Ravaillac.
politics.context: It happened in May.

society.text: Spanish settlers found Santa Fe, in what is now New Mexico, one of the oldest European towns in the United States.
society.context: Pedro de Peralta founded it as the colony's capital.

technology.text: The Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei discovers four moons orbiting Jupiter and publishes the news in The Starry Messenger.
technology.context: He first saw them in January.

arts_culture.text: The Italian painter Caravaggio, famous for his dramatic light and shadow, dies on the Tuscan coast while travelling to Rome.

politics.text: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden is killed leading a cavalry charge at the Battle of Lützen, in the Thirty Years' War.
politics.context: He died in November, though his army won the battle.

society.text: Swedish rulers found the University of Tartu, in what is now Estonia.
society.context: It was founded in June, as the Academia Gustaviana.

technology.text: The Italian scientist Galileo Galilei publishes his Dialogue about the two chief world systems, defending a Sun-centred universe.
technology.context: It led to his trial for heresy the following year.

arts_culture.text: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan begins building the Taj Mahal, at Agra, as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
arts_culture.context: Work began soon after her death the year before.

politics.text: Christian peasants rise against heavy taxes at Shimabara, in Japan, in a revolt the shogunate will crush the next year.
politics.context: The Shimabara Rebellion began late in the year.

society.text: Tulip prices collapse in the Dutch Republic, ending a speculative frenzy among traders in Amsterdam and Haarlem.
society.context: Tulip mania peaked over the winter and crashed in February. Historians now debate how widespread it was.

technology.text: The French philosopher René Descartes publishes Discourse on Method, setting out his approach to scientific reasoning.
technology.context: It was printed in Leiden, in the Dutch Republic, in June.

arts_culture.text: The French playwright Pierre Corneille's tragicomedy Le Cid premieres in Paris and sparks a bitter literary quarrel.
arts_culture.context: It opened at the very start of the year. The exact date is uncertain.

politics.text: King Charles I raises his standard at Nottingham, and civil war breaks out between his supporters and Parliament.
politics.context: The English Civil War began in August.

society.text: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman becomes the first European to sight the island later named Tasmania.
society.context: He sighted it in November, and went on to find New Zealand.

technology.text: The French teenager Blaise Pascal invents a mechanical calculator to help his tax-collector father.
technology.context: He began work on the Pascaline this year, at the age of eighteen.

arts_culture.text: The Dutch painter Rembrandt completes The Night Watch, a huge group portrait of an Amsterdam militia company.
arts_culture.context: It was completed in the middle of the year.

politics.text: Treaties signed at Münster and Osnabrück end the Thirty Years' War and reshape the borders of the Holy Roman Empire.
politics.context: The Peace of Westphalia was agreed in October.

society.text: Cossacks led by Bohdan Khmelnytsky rise against Polish nobles in what is now Ukraine.
society.context: The Khmelnytsky Uprising began in the spring and reshaped eastern Europe.

technology.text: The Cossack explorer Semyon Dezhnev sails round the north-eastern tip of Asia, through the strait later named after Bering.
technology.context: Almost nobody heard of the voyage for decades.

technology.text: At Blaise Pascal's request, his brother-in-law carries a barometer up the Puy de Dôme, showing that air pressure falls with height.
technology.context: The experiment was in September.

arts_culture.text: The white marble mausoleum built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal is completed at Agra.
arts_culture.context: This is the main tomb of the Taj Mahal. The wider complex took several more years.

arts_culture.text: The Royal Academy of Painting and Sculpture is founded in Paris, as a school for the king's artists.

politics.text: The Maratha leader Shivaji escapes from house arrest at Emperor Aurangzeb's court in Agra, reputedly in a basket of sweets.
politics.context: He slipped away in August and returned to the Deccan.

society.text: A fire that starts in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane destroys most of the City of London.
society.context: The Great Fire of London burned for four days in September.

technology.text: King Louis XIV's minister Jean-Baptiste Colbert founds the Académie des sciences in Paris.
technology.context: It was set up in December.

arts_culture.text: The French playwright Molière's comedy The Misanthrope, about a man who hates hypocrisy, opens in Paris.
The Dutch painter Frans Hals, famous for his lively portraits, dies in Haarlem.

politics.text: The Qing navy under Admiral Shi Lang defeats the Zheng regime and takes Taiwan for China.
politics.context: The Zheng family's kingdom on the island surrendered in the late summer.

politics.text: A relief army led by King Jan III Sobieski of Poland routs the Ottoman besiegers of Vienna.
politics.context: The Battle of Vienna was fought in September.

society.text: The Ashmolean Museum opens in Oxford, the first university museum in the world.
society.context: It opened in May, built around the collection of Elias Ashmole.

technology.text: The Dutch microscopist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek describes tiny living creatures, later called bacteria, scraped from teeth.
technology.context: He described them in a letter to the Royal Society in September.

arts_culture.text: The English composer Henry Purcell writes an ode for the feast of Saint Cecilia, patron saint of music, in London.
arts_culture.context: The ode was Welcome to All the Pleasures. It was first performed in November.

politics.text: The Ottoman army is crushed at the Second Battle of Mohács, in Hungary, by the forces of the Holy Roman Empire.
politics.context: It was fought in August.

society.text: A Venetian shell hits an Ottoman gunpowder store inside the Parthenon, in Athens, and blows the roof off the ancient temple.
society.context: The explosion was in September.

technology.text: The English scientist Isaac Newton publishes the Principia, setting out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.
technology.context: It was published in July.

arts_culture.text: The Italian-born French composer Jean-Baptiste Lully dies in Paris after striking his foot with his conducting staff.
arts_culture.context: He died in March, of gangrene.

politics.text: Aurangzeb, the last great Mughal emperor, dies in Ahmednagar, and his empire begins to fall apart.
politics.context: He died in March after almost fifty years on the throne.

politics.text: England and Scotland unite as the Kingdom of Great Britain under the Acts of Union.
politics.context: The Union took effect on the first of May.

society.text: A huge earthquake shakes Japan, and weeks later Mount Fuji erupts for the last time in recorded history.
society.context: The Hōei earthquake struck in October. Fuji erupted in December.

technology.text: The French physicist Denis Papin sails a small steam-driven paddle boat on the River Fulda, in Germany.
technology.context: Local boatmen are said to have smashed the boat soon afterwards.

arts_culture.text: The Danish-German organist Dieterich Buxtehude, whom the young Bach once walked miles to hear, dies in Lübeck.
arts_culture.context: He died in May. Bach had visited him two years earlier.

politics.text: Diplomats gather at Utrecht, in the Dutch Republic, to negotiate an end to the War of the Spanish Succession.
politics.context: The congress opened in January.

society.text: A court in Hertfordshire convicts Jane Wenham of witchcraft, the last such conviction in England.
society.context: The judge secured her pardon soon afterwards.

technology.text: The English inventor Thomas Newcomen installs the first practical steam engine, to pump water out of a coal mine near Dudley.
technology.context: It was installed at the Conygree coalworks.

arts_culture.text: The English poet Alexander Pope publishes the first version of The Rape of the Lock, a mock-heroic poem about a stolen curl of hair.
arts_culture.context: A longer version followed two years later.

politics.text: The Persian ruler Nader Shah sacks Delhi, taking the Peacock Throne and vast treasure from the Mughal Empire.
politics.context: He took the city in March.

society.text: Enslaved people rise in the Stono Rebellion near Charleston, South Carolina, the largest slave revolt in the British mainland colonies.
society.context: It began in September.

technology.text: The French engineer Jacques de Vaucanson shows a mechanical duck that appears to eat, digest and excrete grain.
technology.context: He showed it in Paris.

arts_culture.text: George Frideric Handel's oratorio Israel in Egypt is first performed in London.

politics.text: General Edward Braddock's British army is ambushed and routed by French and Native American forces near the Monongahela River.
politics.context: The battle was fought in July.

society.text: A huge earthquake, tsunami and fire destroy much of Lisbon, the Portuguese capital, on All Saints' Day.
society.context: It struck on the first of November.

technology.text: The German philosopher Immanuel Kant proposes that the solar system formed from a spinning cloud of gas and dust.
technology.context: He published the idea anonymously.

arts_culture.text: The English writer Samuel Johnson publishes A Dictionary of the English Language, after nearly nine years of work.

politics.text: Hyder Ali of Mysore dictates peace terms to the British outside Madras, ending the First Anglo-Mysore War.
politics.context: The Treaty of Madras was signed in April.

society.text: The Spanish Franciscan friar Junípero Serra founds Mission San Diego, the first of the California missions.
society.context: He founded it in July.

technology.text: The Scottish engineer James Watt patents a steam engine with a separate condenser, far more efficient than earlier engines.
technology.context: The patent was granted in January.

technology.text: Captain James Cook observes the transit of Venus from Tahiti, before sailing on to chart the coast of New Zealand.
technology.context: He observed the transit in June, on his first voyage in the Endeavour.

arts_culture.text: The Royal Academy of Arts, with Joshua Reynolds as its first president, holds its first exhibition in London.
arts_culture.context: The exhibition opened in April. The Academy had been founded the previous December.

politics.text: A British army under Lord Cornwallis surrenders to American and French forces at Yorktown, Virginia.
politics.context: The surrender was in October.

society.text: The Austrian emperor Joseph II grants Protestants and Orthodox Christians the right to worship in his lands.
society.context: He issued the Patent of Toleration in October.

technology.text: The British astronomer William Herschel discovers a new planet, Uranus, using a telescope he built himself, in Bath.
technology.context: He found it in March.

arts_culture.text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera Idomeneo premieres in Munich.

politics.text: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue launch a revolt that grows into the Haitian Revolution.
politics.context: It began in August in the north of the island.

politics.text: King Louis XVI and his family are caught at Varennes while trying to flee revolutionary Paris.
politics.context: The flight to Varennes was in June.

society.text: The young United States ratifies the Bill of Rights, ten amendments protecting individual freedoms.
society.context: The ratification was completed in December.

technology.text: The Italian scientist Luigi Galvani publishes his findings on electricity in the muscles of frogs.
technology.context: His work on "animal electricity" led Alessandro Volta to build the first battery.

arts_culture.text: Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's fairy-tale opera The Magic Flute premieres in a suburban theatre in Vienna.
arts_culture.context: It opened in September. Mozart died in December.

politics.text: Revolutionary France wins its first great victory at Valmy, and the National Convention declares France a republic.
politics.context: Valmy was fought on the twentieth of September.

society.text: The English writer Mary Wollstonecraft publishes A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, arguing that women deserve an education.
society.context: It came out in January.

technology.text: The Scottish engineer William Murdoch lights his house in Redruth, in Cornwall, with gas made from coal.
technology.context: He lit the house in the early part of the 1790s.

arts_culture.text: A French army officer, Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle, writes a marching song in Strasbourg that becomes the French national anthem.

politics.text: King Louis XVI of France is executed by guillotine in Paris.
politics.context: He was executed in January.

society.text: The Committee of Public Safety begins the Reign of Terror in France, as thousands go to the guillotine.
society.context: It was declared in September.

technology.text: The American inventor Eli Whitney builds a machine that quickly separates cotton fibres from their seeds, the cotton gin.
technology.context: He built it in Georgia and patented it the next year.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Jacques-Louis David completes The Death of Marat, showing the murdered revolutionary in his bath.
arts_culture.context: It was painted in the months after the killing in July.

politics.text: Napoleon Bonaparte lands a French army in Egypt, hoping to threaten British India.
politics.context: He landed near Alexandria in July and won the Battle of the Pyramids.

politics.text: Admiral Horatio Nelson destroys the French fleet at the Battle of the Nile, in Aboukir Bay, off Egypt.
politics.context: The battle was fought in early August, cutting off Napoleon's army in Egypt.

society.text: The English clergyman Thomas Malthus publishes An Essay on the Principle of Population, warning that people will outrun food.
society.context: It first appeared anonymously.

technology.text: The English doctor Edward Jenner publishes his study showing that cowpox inoculation protects against smallpox.
technology.context: He had tested the idea on a boy, James Phipps, two years earlier.

arts_culture.text: The English poets William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge publish Lyrical Ballads, a landmark of Romanticism.
arts_culture.context: It appeared anonymously in the autumn.

politics.text: British forces storm Seringapatam, in southern India, and kill Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore.
politics.context: The city fell in May, ending the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

politics.text: Napoleon Bonaparte seizes power in a coup in Paris and becomes First Consul of France.
politics.context: The coup took place in November.

society.text: The German naturalist Alexander von Humboldt sets sail from Spain on a five-year scientific expedition to Latin America.
society.context: He left A Coruña in June with the botanist Aimé Bonpland.

technology.text: French soldiers digging a fort near Rashid, in Egypt, uncover a stone carved in three scripts that will unlock hieroglyphs.
technology.context: The Rosetta Stone was found in July.

arts_culture.text: Ludwig van Beethoven publishes his Pathétique piano sonata in Vienna.
arts_culture.context: Beethoven was in his late twenties.

politics.text: Napoleon Bonaparte's army defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Marengo, in northern Italy.
politics.context: It was fought in June.

society.text: The United States Congress founds the Library of Congress, as a small collection for lawmakers in the new capital.
society.context: It was founded in April. It later grew into one of the largest libraries in the world.

technology.text: The Italian physicist Alessandro Volta announces the voltaic pile, the first electric battery.
technology.context: He announced it in a letter to the Royal Society in March.

arts_culture.text: Ludwig van Beethoven conducts the premiere of his first symphony in Vienna.

politics.text: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declares Haiti independent, taking back its Indigenous Taíno name and forming the first free Black republic.
politics.context: The declaration was made on New Year's Day.

politics.text: Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French, in Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris.
politics.context: The coronation was in December. Pope Pius VII looked on.

society.text: The American explorers Meriwether Lewis and William Clark set out up the Missouri River from St. Louis to find a route to the Pacific.
society.context: They left in May and reached the Pacific coast the following year.

technology.text: Richard Trevithick's steam locomotive hauls iron and passengers along a tramway at Merthyr Tydfil, in Wales.
technology.context: The first run took place in February.

arts_culture.text: The German dramatist Friedrich Schiller's play Wilhelm Tell, about a Swiss archer who defies a tyrant, is first staged in Weimar.

politics.text: Portugal's royal court flees Napoleon's invading army and sails from Lisbon for Brazil, soon making Rio de Janeiro its capital.
politics.context: The fleet left in November and reached Brazil early the next year.

politics.text: The British navy bombards Copenhagen and seizes the Danish fleet, to stop it falling into Napoleon's hands.
politics.context: The attack was in September.

society.text: The British Parliament passes an act abolishing the slave trade throughout the British Empire.
society.context: The Slave Trade Act received royal assent in March. Slavery itself continued until later.

technology.text: The American inventor Robert Fulton's steamboat makes its first run up the Hudson River from New York City to Albany.
technology.context: The trip began in August and took about thirty-two hours.

arts_culture.text: The young English poet Lord Byron publishes his first book of verse, Hours of Idleness.
arts_culture.context: A harsh review of it provoked his satire English Bards and Scotch Reviewers.

politics.text: The Mexican priest Miguel Hidalgo rings his church bell at Dolores and calls on his parish to rise against Spanish rule.
politics.context: The Cry of Dolores came in September and began the Mexican War of Independence.

society.text: Munich celebrates the wedding of Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria with horse races and a huge public party that becomes a yearly tradition.
society.context: It was the first Oktoberfest, held in October.

technology.text: The French confectioner Nicolas Appert publishes his method of preserving food in sealed glass jars.
technology.context: He had won a prize from Napoleon's government for the method.

arts_culture.text: The Scottish writer Walter Scott publishes The Lady of the Lake, a romantic poem set in the Highlands, and it becomes a bestseller.

politics.text: The United States declares war on Britain, beginning a three-year conflict over trade, impressment and expansion.
politics.context: Congress voted for war in June. The conflict is known by the year it began.

society.text: Fires burn much of Moscow as Napoleon's army occupies the Russian city.
society.context: The fires started in September.

technology.text: The Scottish engineer Henry Bell launches the paddle steamer Comet on the River Clyde, the first successful commercial steamboat in Europe.
technology.context: It began carrying passengers in August.

arts_culture.text: The German brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm publish the first volume of their collected fairy tales.

politics.text: General Andrew Jackson's American troops defeat a larger British force outside New Orleans, after a peace treaty is already signed.
politics.context: The battle was fought in January. News of the Treaty of Ghent had not yet arrived.

politics.text: Napoleon Bonaparte is defeated by the Duke of Wellington and Marshal Blücher at the Battle of Waterloo, in Belgium.
politics.context: The battle was fought in June.

politics.text: The Congress of Vienna ends, redrawing the map of Europe after the defeat of Napoleon.
politics.context: Its final act was signed in June.

society.text: Mount Tambora erupts on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa, the most powerful eruption in recorded history.
society.context: It erupted in April. The following year was known as the "year without a summer".

technology.text: The English chemist Humphry Davy invents a safety lamp that will not ignite the gas in coal mines.
technology.context: It cut the number of deaths from firedamp explosions.

arts_culture.text: The English novelist Jane Austen publishes Emma, a comedy about a matchmaking young woman in a country village.
arts_culture.context: It came out in December. The title page is dated the following year.

politics.text: José de San Martín declares Peru independent from Spain in Lima.
politics.context: He declared it in July. Spanish forces held out in the mountains for years.

politics.text: Greek rebels rise against Ottoman rule, beginning the Greek War of Independence.
politics.context: The revolt began in March.

society.text: Free Black Americans, backed by the American Colonization Society, acquire land at Cape Mesurado to found the colony of Liberia.
society.context: The land was acquired in December. The first settlers arrived early the next year.

technology.text: The English scientist Michael Faraday builds the first device that turns electricity into continuous motion.
technology.context: It was a forerunner of the electric motor. He demonstrated it in the autumn.

arts_culture.text: The German composer Carl Maria von Weber's opera Der Freischütz premieres in Berlin and launches German Romantic opera.

politics.text: Patriots known as the Thirty-Three Orientals declare independence for the territory of Uruguay from Brazil.
politics.context: The declaration was in August.

society.text: The Erie Canal opens, linking the Hudson River to the Great Lakes across New York State.
society.context: It opened in October.

technology.text: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens in northern England, the first public railway to use steam locomotives.
technology.context: George Stephenson's engine pulled the first train in September.

arts_culture.text: The French lawyer Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin publishes The Physiology of Taste, a famous book about food and dining.

politics.text: France invades Algiers, beginning a conquest of North Africa that will last for decades.
politics.context: The French landed in June and the city fell in July.

politics.text: Parisians fight for three days in the July Revolution, forcing King Charles X of France to abdicate.
politics.context: The "Three Glorious Days" were in late July.

society.text: The American Joseph Smith founds a church in upstate New York that grows into the Latter Day Saint movement.
society.context: He founded it in April, a month after publishing the Book of Mormon.

technology.text: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway, the first intercity line run entirely by steam locomotives, opens in England.
technology.context: It opened in September. The politician William Huskisson was killed by a train on opening day.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Eugène Delacroix paints Liberty Leading the People, celebrating the July Revolution in Paris.
arts_culture.context: He painted it in the autumn. It was first shown the following year.

politics.text: Eighteen-year-old Victoria becomes queen of the United Kingdom on the death of her uncle, King William IV.
politics.context: She became queen in June.

society.text: A financial panic spreads from New York as banks stop paying out, and the American economy slides into depression.
society.context: The Panic of 1837 began in May.

technology.text: In Britain, William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone patent the first commercial electric telegraph.
technology.context: They patented it in June.

arts_culture.text: The Danish author Hans Christian Andersen publishes The Little Mermaid.
arts_culture.context: It appeared in a collection of his fairy tales in the spring.

politics.text: The Chinese official Lin Zexu destroys thousands of chests of seized British opium at Humen, near Canton.
politics.context: The opium was destroyed in June. Britain sent a fleet the following year.

society.text: The Ottoman sultan's Edict of Gülhane promises equal treatment for all his subjects and begins the Tanzimat reforms.
society.context: It was issued in November in the name of Sultan Abdulmejid I.

technology.text: The French artist Louis Daguerre's photographic process, the daguerreotype, is announced and given free to the world by France.
technology.context: It was announced in January and the details revealed in August.

technology.text: The American inventor Charles Goodyear discovers how to harden rubber by heating it with sulphur, in a process called vulcanisation.
technology.context: He found the process by accident.

arts_culture.text: The English painter J. M. W. Turner exhibits The Fighting Temeraire, showing an old warship being towed to its last berth.
arts_culture.context: It was shown at the Royal Academy in May.

politics.text: Maori chiefs and British officials sign the Treaty of Waitangi at the Bay of Islands.
politics.context: It was signed in February, in what is now New Zealand.

society.text: Britain issues the Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp, as part of a postal reform led by Rowland Hill.
society.context: It went on sale in May.

society.text: Queen Victoria marries her cousin Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha, in London.
society.context: They married in February.

technology.text: The American inventor Samuel Morse receives a patent for his electric telegraph.
technology.context: The patent was granted in June. His famous first public message followed four years later.

arts_culture.text: The German composer Robert Schumann writes the song cycle Dichterliebe, in a burst of song-writing after marrying Clara Wieck.
arts_culture.context: He married in September, and wrote more than a hundred songs this year.

politics.text: Britain and China sign the Treaty of Nanking, ending the First Opium War and handing over Hong Kong island.
politics.context: It was signed in August aboard a British warship.

society.text: The Illustrated London News publishes its first issue, as the world's first illustrated weekly newspaper.
society.context: It first appeared in May.

technology.text: The American doctor Crawford Long uses ether to put a patient to sleep for an operation, in Jefferson, Georgia.
technology.context: He operated in March.

arts_culture.text: The Russian writer Nikolai Gogol publishes Dead Souls, a satirical novel about a swindler who buys dead serfs.

politics.text: Revolutions spread across Europe, beginning in Sicily and Paris, and toppling King Louis-Philippe of France.
politics.context: The unrest began in January and February.

society.text: Delegates meet at Seneca Falls, in New York, for the first women's rights convention in the United States.
society.context: It was held in July.

technology.text: The British physicist William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin, proposes an absolute temperature scale with a lowest possible temperature.
technology.context: He proposed it in a paper that year.

arts_culture.text: A group of young English painters founds the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in London, led by Dante Gabriel Rossetti and John Everett Millais.

politics.text: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace in China's Guangxi province, launching the Taiping Rebellion.
politics.context: The revolt began in January and became one of the deadliest wars in history.

society.text: Queen Victoria opens the Great Exhibition in a huge glass hall, the Crystal Palace, in London's Hyde Park.
society.context: It opened in May.

technology.text: The American inventor Isaac Singer patents a sewing machine that makes sewing at home practical.
technology.context: He patented it in August.

arts_culture.text: The American writer Herman Melville publishes Moby-Dick, a novel about a whaling captain's obsession.
arts_culture.context: It came out in the autumn and sold poorly at first.

politics.text: American Commodore Matthew Perry sails his black ships into Edo Bay, demanding that Japan open to trade.
politics.context: He arrived in July.

society.text: Baron Haussmann is appointed to rebuild Paris, and begins carving wide boulevards through the old city.
society.context: He was appointed in June by Napoleon III.

technology.text: The English engineer Sir George Cayley's glider carries a man across a valley in Yorkshire, perhaps the first manned glider flight.
technology.context: The passenger was reportedly his coachman.

arts_culture.text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera La traviata, based on a play by Alexandre Dumas the younger, premieres in Venice.
arts_culture.context: It premiered in March and was a failure at first.

politics.text: Indian soldiers in the East India Company's army mutiny at Meerut, and the revolt spreads across northern India.
politics.context: It began in May and ended Company rule.

society.text: The US Supreme Court rules in Dred Scott v. Sandford that a man born into slavery cannot be an American citizen.
society.context: The decision came in March and deepened the divide before the Civil War.

technology.text: Elisha Otis installs the first safe passenger lift in the Haughwout department store in New York.
technology.context: It went in during March.

technology.text: The French chemist Louis Pasteur shows that fermentation is caused by living yeast, a step towards germ theory.
technology.context: He published the finding in Lille.

arts_culture.text: The French poet Charles Baudelaire publishes Les Fleurs du mal, and is then prosecuted for offending public morals.
arts_culture.context: It came out in June. Six poems were banned.

arts_culture.text: The French novelist Gustave Flaubert publishes Madame Bovary, a story of provincial adultery, after being tried for obscenity.
arts_culture.context: He was acquitted in February, and the novel came out as a book in April.

politics.text: The abolitionist John Brown leads a raid on the federal armoury at Harpers Ferry, Virginia, hoping to start a slave uprising.
politics.context: The raid took place in October. Brown was hanged soon after.

politics.text: France and Piedmont-Sardinia defeat Austria at the Battle of Solferino, in the Second Italian War of Independence.
politics.context: It was fought in June. Its horrors inspired Henry Dunant to found the Red Cross.

society.text: A huge solar storm, later named for the British astronomer Richard Carrington, sets telegraph offices alight across the world.
society.context: It hit in early September and lit up the night sky as far south as the Caribbean.

technology.text: The English naturalist Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species, arguing that species evolve by natural selection.
technology.context: It came out in November.

technology.text: Work begins on the Suez Canal, under the French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps.
technology.context: Digging began in April. The canal took ten years to build.

arts_culture.text: The English novelist Charles Dickens finishes the weekly serial of A Tale of Two Cities, set in London and Paris.
arts_culture.context: It ran from April to November.

arts_culture.text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera A Masked Ball premieres in Rome, after censors force changes to the plot.

politics.text: President Abraham Lincoln issues the Emancipation Proclamation, declaring enslaved people in the rebel states to be free.
politics.context: It took effect on New Year's Day.

society.text: Football clubs meet in a London tavern and form the Football Association, laying down the first common rules of the game.
society.context: They met in October.

technology.text: The world's first underground railway, the Metropolitan Railway, opens in London.
technology.context: It opened in January.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Édouard Manet shows Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe at the Salon des Refusés, in Paris, and causes a scandal.

politics.text: Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay sign the Treaty of the Triple Alliance against Paraguay.
politics.context: It was signed in May, during the Paraguayan War.

politics.text: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrenders to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia.
politics.context: The surrender was in April.

society.text: The American states ratify the Thirteenth Amendment, abolishing slavery across the United States.
society.context: It was ratified in December, after the end of the Civil War.

technology.text: The Austrian monk Gregor Mendel presents his experiments on pea plants to a natural history society in Brno.
technology.context: He read his papers in February and March. His work was ignored until after the turn of the century.

arts_culture.text: The English author Lewis Carroll publishes Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, with drawings by John Tenniel.
arts_culture.context: It first appeared in November. The first printing was withdrawn and reissued.

politics.text: Britain's North American colonies unite as the Dominion of Canada.
politics.context: Confederation took place on the first of July.

society.text: The German thinker Karl Marx publishes the first volume of Das Kapital, his study of capitalism.
society.context: It was published in September.

technology.text: The Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel patents dynamite, a safe and stable explosive.
technology.context: He patented it in Britain and Sweden.

arts_culture.text: The Austrian composer Johann Strauss the Younger's waltz The Blue Danube premieres in Vienna.

politics.text: Pro-shogun forces surrender at Hakodate, on the northern Japanese island of Hokkaido, ending the Boshin War.
politics.context: The war ended in May. It cleared the way for the Meiji government.

society.text: A golden spike is driven at Promontory Summit, Utah, joining the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads across America.
society.context: It was done in May, completing the first transcontinental railroad.

technology.text: The Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev arranges the known elements by atomic weight and publishes his periodic table.
technology.context: He published it in March and left gaps for elements not yet found.

technology.text: The Suez Canal opens, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and cutting the sea route from Europe to Asia.
technology.context: It opened in November, with a grand ceremony attended by Empress Eugénie of France.

arts_culture.text: The Russian count Leo Tolstoy completes War and Peace, his vast novel about families and Napoleon's invasion of Russia.

politics.text: King Wilhelm of Prussia is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
politics.context: It happened in January, as France was losing the Franco-Prussian War.

politics.text: Radical Parisians proclaim the Paris Commune after the French defeat by Prussia.
politics.context: The Commune was proclaimed in March and crushed that May.

society.text: A fire that starts in a barn spreads through Chicago and burns for days, destroying much of the city.
society.context: The Great Chicago Fire began in October.

technology.text: Charles Darwin publishes The Descent of Man, applying his theory of natural selection to human origins.
technology.context: It came out in February.

arts_culture.text: Giuseppe Verdi's opera Aida, set in ancient Egypt, premieres at the Khedivial Opera House in Cairo.

politics.text: Benjamin Disraeli becomes British prime minister after the Conservatives win a general election.
politics.context: He took office in February.

society.text: The explorer Henry Morton Stanley sets out from Zanzibar on an expedition across central Africa.
society.context: He left in November. The journey took nearly three years.

technology.text: The American farmer Joseph Glidden patents barbed wire, which changes the way the Great Plains are farmed.
technology.context: He patented it in November.

arts_culture.text: A group of French artists, including Claude Monet and Pierre-Auguste Renoir, hold the first Impressionist exhibition in Paris.

politics.text: The Ottoman Empire adopts its first written constitution and opens a parliament in Constantinople.
politics.context: The constitution was proclaimed in December. The sultan suspended it within two years.

society.text: Lakota and Cheyenne warriors wipe out Lieutenant Colonel George Custer's US cavalry column at the Little Bighorn, in Montana.
society.context: The battle was fought in June.

technology.text: The Scottish-born inventor Alexander Graham Bell is granted a patent for the telephone in the United States.
technology.context: The patent was granted in March.

technology.text: The German engineer Nikolaus Otto builds the first practical four-stroke internal combustion engine.
technology.context: His design became the basis of most petrol engines.

arts_culture.text: Richard Wagner's four-opera Ring cycle is staged complete for the first time at his new opera house in Bayreuth, Germany.
arts_culture.context: It opened the first Bayreuth Festival in August.

politics.text: Queen Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India at a grand durbar in Delhi.
politics.context: The proclamation was on New Year's Day.

society.text: A railway workers' strike spreads across the United States, with riots in Pittsburgh and other cities.
society.context: It began in July.

technology.text: The American inventor Thomas Edison builds the first phonograph, a machine that records and plays back sound.
technology.context: He demonstrated it in December.

arts_culture.text: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky's ballet Swan Lake premieres at the Bolshoi Theatre, in Moscow.
arts_culture.context: It opened in March, to a poor reception.

politics.text: A Zulu army wipes out a British column at Isandlwana, in southern Africa.
politics.context: It was fought in January, at the start of the Anglo-Zulu War.

society.text: A railway bridge across the Firth of Tay, in Scotland, collapses in a storm as a train crosses it, killing everyone on board.
society.context: The Tay Bridge disaster happened late in December.

technology.text: The American inventor Thomas Edison perfects a long-lasting electric light bulb at Menlo Park, New Jersey.
technology.context: His first long-lasting lamp worked in October.

arts_culture.text: The Norwegian playwright Henrik Ibsen's A Doll's House premieres in Copenhagen and shocks audiences with its ending.

politics.text: Revolutionaries assassinate Tsar Alexander II of Russia with a bomb in Saint Petersburg.
politics.context: He was killed in March.

society.text: Lawmen and outlaws fight a famous gunfight at the O.K. Corral, in Tombstone, Arizona.
society.context: It happened in October.

technology.text: The German firm Siemens opens the world's first electric tram line, in Lichterfelde, near Berlin.
technology.context: It opened in May.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir paints Luncheon of the Boating Party, a lively scene of friends on a balcony above the Seine.
arts_culture.context: He finished it after working on it for a year.

politics.text: France forces the Treaty of Huế on the Vietnamese emperor, making central and northern Vietnam French protectorates.
politics.context: It was signed in August.

society.text: The volcanic island of Krakatoa, between Java and Sumatra, explodes in one of the loudest sounds in recorded history.
society.context: It erupted in August. Its tsunamis killed tens of thousands.

technology.text: The Brooklyn Bridge, with its stone towers and steel cables, opens between New York City and Brooklyn.
technology.context: It opened in May.

arts_culture.text: The German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche publishes the first part of Thus Spoke Zarathustra, a prose poem about a prophet.
arts_culture.context: He wrote it in a matter of days while living in Italy.

arts_culture.text: The Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson publishes Treasure Island as a book, a pirate adventure narrated by the boy Jim Hawkins.

politics.text: The forces of the Mahdi capture Khartoum, in Sudan, and kill the British General Charles Gordon.
politics.context: The city fell in January after a siege of ten months.

politics.text: European powers end the Berlin Conference, agreeing rules for carving up African territory among themselves.
politics.context: The conference closed in February. Not one African ruler had been invited.

society.text: The Statue of Liberty arrives in New York Harbor from France, packed in more than two hundred crates.
society.context: It arrived in June. Its pedestal was not finished until the following year.

technology.text: The German engineer Karl Benz builds a three-wheeled motor car with a petrol engine, a forerunner of the modern car.
technology.context: He built it this year and patented it in January of the next.

arts_culture.text: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado, set in Japan, opens in London.
arts_culture.context: It opened in March and became their most popular work.

politics.text: The Apache leader Geronimo surrenders to the United States Army in Arizona, ending the last major Indian war.
politics.context: He surrendered in September.

society.text: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated by President Grover Cleveland in New York Harbor.
society.context: The dedication was in October.

technology.text: The German engineer Karl Benz receives a patent for his motor car, the first for a practical petrol-driven vehicle.
technology.context: The patent was granted in January.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Georges Seurat exhibits A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte, made of thousands of tiny dots of colour.
arts_culture.context: It was shown at the last Impressionist exhibition.

politics.text: Brazil's Princess Isabel signs the Golden Law, abolishing slavery.
politics.context: She signed it in May. Brazil was the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery.

politics.text: Wilhelm II becomes German emperor in the Year of the Three Emperors, after the deaths of his grandfather and father.
politics.context: He took the throne in June.

society.text: A huge blizzard paralyses New York and the American north-east, burying cities in snow for days.
society.context: It struck in March.

technology.text: George Eastman launches the Kodak camera, a simple box camera that anyone can use.
technology.context: The trademark was registered in the autumn. The slogan was "You press the button, we do the rest".

technology.text: The Serbian-American inventor Nikola Tesla patents his alternating-current motor and power system.
technology.context: The patents were granted in May and later used by George Westinghouse.

arts_culture.text: The Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh moves to Arles, in the south of France, where he paints his sunflowers and his yellow house.

politics.text: Emperor Meiji grants Japan its first modern constitution, creating an elected parliament.
politics.context: The constitution was proclaimed in February.

society.text: A dam above Johnstown, Pennsylvania, collapses after heavy rain, and the flood kills more than two thousand people.
society.context: It happened in May.

technology.text: The engineer Gustave Eiffel's tower is finished in Paris for the World's Fair, making it the tallest structure in the world.
technology.context: It was completed in March.

arts_culture.text: The Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh paints The Starry Night while staying in an asylum at Saint-Rémy, in southern France.

politics.text: France and Russia agree a friendship that grows into an alliance, bringing together two rivals of Germany.
politics.context: The first agreement was in August.

society.text: The Canadian-American teacher James Naismith invents basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts.
society.context: He invented it in December, using peach baskets.

technology.text: Russia begins building the Trans-Siberian Railway, to link Moscow with the Pacific port of Vladivostok.
technology.context: Construction began in May.

arts_culture.text: The Irish writer Oscar Wilde publishes The Picture of Dorian Gray as a book, a novel about a man whose portrait ages in his place.
arts_culture.context: It came out in the spring.

politics.text: Japan and China go to war over control of Korea, in the First Sino-Japanese War.
politics.context: War was declared in August.

society.text: Pierre de Coubertin founds the International Olympic Committee at a congress in Paris.
society.context: It was founded in June.

technology.text: Tower Bridge opens across the River Thames in London, with a middle section that lifts to let ships through.
technology.context: It opened in June.

arts_culture.text: Claude Debussy's Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun premieres in Paris.

politics.text: Japan and China sign the Treaty of Shimonoseki, ending their war, and China gives Taiwan to Japan.
politics.context: It was signed in April.

society.text: The Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel signs his will, leaving his fortune to fund prizes in his name.
society.context: He signed it in November.

technology.text: The German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays in his laboratory in Würzburg.
technology.context: He found them in November.

arts_culture.text: The French brothers Auguste and Louis Lumière show a film to a paying audience, in a Paris café.
arts_culture.context: It was shown on the twenty-eighth of December.

politics.text: Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II crush an Italian army at Adwa, securing Ethiopia's independence.
politics.context: The battle was fought on the first of March.

society.text: The first modern Olympic Games open in Athens, the Greek city where the ancient ones began.
society.context: They opened in April, with athletes from fourteen countries.

technology.text: The French physicist Henri Becquerel finds that uranium salts fog photographic plates in the dark, revealing radioactivity.
technology.context: He made the discovery in Paris, in the early part of the year.

technology.text: The Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi applies in Britain for the first patent on a wireless telegraph system.
technology.context: He filed the application in June. The patent was granted the following year.

arts_culture.text: Giacomo Puccini's opera La Bohème, about young artists in Paris, opens in Turin, conducted by Arturo Toscanini.
Anton Chekhov's play The Seagull premieres in St Petersburg, to a hostile audience.
arts_culture.context: The first night in October was a disaster. A later production by Stanislavski made it a triumph.

politics.text: Theodor Herzl opens the first Zionist Congress in Basel, Switzerland.
politics.context: It opened in August.

society.text: Gold is found in the Klondike region of Canada, setting off a rush of prospectors to the Yukon.
society.context: The news reached the cities in July.

technology.text: The British physicist J. J. Thomson announces the discovery of the electron, the first subatomic particle.
technology.context: He announced it in April.

arts_culture.text: The Irish writer Bram Stoker publishes the vampire novel Dracula.

politics.text: Reformers around the Chinese emperor Guangxu launch the Hundred Days' Reform, until Empress Dowager Cixi crushes it.
politics.context: It ran from June to September.

politics.text: The United States declares war on Spain over Cuba, beginning the Spanish-American War.
politics.context: The declaration was in April.

society.text: The American battleship USS Maine explodes in Havana harbour, killing hundreds of sailors and pushing America towards war with Spain.
society.context: It exploded in February. The cause was long disputed.

technology.text: In Paris, Marie and Pierre Curie announce the discovery of two new radioactive elements, polonium and radium.
technology.context: Polonium was announced in July and radium in December.

arts_culture.text: The French novelist Émile Zola publishes an open letter in a Paris newspaper accusing the army of a miscarriage of justice.
arts_culture.context: It is known as J'accuse and appeared in January, in L'Aurore, over the Dreyfus affair.

politics.text: Chinese Boxer fighters and imperial troops besiege the foreign legations in Beijing, as an eight-nation force marches to relieve them.
politics.context: The siege lasted from June to August.

society.text: A hurricane destroys the Texas port city of Galveston, in the deadliest natural disaster in American history.
society.context: It struck in September.

technology.text: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin flies his first rigid airship over Lake Constance, in Germany.
technology.context: It flew in July.

technology.text: The German physicist Max Planck proposes that energy comes in tiny packets, laying the foundations of quantum theory.
technology.context: He presented the idea in Berlin in December.

arts_culture.text: Giacomo Puccini's opera Tosca premieres in Rome.

politics.text: The six Australian colonies join to form the Commonwealth of Australia.
politics.context: Federation took place on New Year's Day.

society.text: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
society.context: They were presented in December.

technology.text: The Italian inventor Guglielmo Marconi receives the first wireless signal sent across the Atlantic Ocean, in Newfoundland.
technology.context: He received the signal in December.

arts_culture.text: The German writer Thomas Mann publishes his first novel, Buddenbrooks, about the decline of a merchant family.

politics.text: Panama breaks away from Colombia with American backing, and the United States gains the right to build a canal.
politics.context: Panama declared independence in November.

politics.text: Russian socialists meet in London and Brussels, and split into Bolsheviks and Mensheviks.
politics.context: The party congress was in the summer.

society.text: The first Tour de France sets off from a café near Paris, with sixty cyclists.
society.context: It began in July. The race was created to sell newspapers.

technology.text: The American brothers Orville and Wilbur Wright make the first powered, controlled flights, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
technology.context: They flew in December. The longest flight that day lasted under a minute.

arts_culture.text: The American writer Jack London publishes The Call of the Wild, a novel about a dog in the Yukon gold rush.
arts_culture.context: It came out in the summer.

politics.text: Japan's navy destroys the Russian fleet at the Battle of Tsushima, a stunning defeat for a European power.
politics.context: It happened in May, during the Russo-Japanese War.

politics.text: Troops fire on a peaceful march of workers in Saint Petersburg on Bloody Sunday, sparking a revolution across Russia.
politics.context: It happened in January.

society.text: The British viceroy Lord Curzon divides the Indian province of Bengal, sparking a nationalist campaign of boycotts.
society.context: The partition took effect in October.

technology.text: Albert Einstein, a young physicist working in a Swiss patent office, publishes papers on relativity and the photoelectric effect.
technology.context: It is known as his "miracle year". He published four landmark papers.

arts_culture.text: A group of French painters led by Henri Matisse, soon nicknamed the "wild beasts", shocks visitors at the Salon d'Automne in Paris.
arts_culture.context: The show was in October. The critic Louis Vauxcelles gave them the name Fauves.

politics.text: Persia's first parliament, the Majlis, opens in Tehran after the Constitutional Revolution forces the shah to agree.
politics.context: It opened in October.

society.text: A huge earthquake and fire destroy much of San Francisco.
society.context: It struck in April.

technology.text: Britain launches HMS Dreadnought, a battleship so powerful that it makes every older warship look outdated.
technology.context: She was launched at Portsmouth in February.

arts_culture.text: The French painter Paul Cézanne, often called the father of modern art, dies in Aix-en-Provence.
arts_culture.context: He died in October, after being caught in a storm while painting.

politics.text: Young Turk army officers force the Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II to restore the constitution.
politics.context: The revolution began in July.

society.text: A huge explosion flattens about two thousand square kilometres of forest in Siberia, near the Tunguska River.
society.context: It happened in June. The cause was probably a meteor exploding in the air.

technology.text: The Ford Motor Company in Detroit introduces the Model T, a cheap and sturdy car designed for ordinary families.
technology.context: It went on sale in October.

arts_culture.text: The Scottish writer Kenneth Grahame publishes The Wind in the Willows, a tale of a Mole, a Rat and a Toad.
The Austrian painter Gustav Klimt completes The Kiss, a couple wrapped in gold leaf, in Vienna.
arts_culture.context: It was shown in Vienna in the summer.

politics.text: Francisco Madero calls for a revolt against Mexican president Porfirio Díaz, beginning the Mexican Revolution.
politics.context: The call to arms came in November.

politics.text: Portugal's monarchy is overthrown in a revolution, and a republic is declared in Lisbon.
politics.context: The revolution was in October.

society.text: Halley's Comet blazes in the night sky and the Earth passes through its tail, causing panic in some places.
society.context: The Earth passed through the tail in May.

technology.text: The French engineer Georges Claude shows the first neon lamp to the public, in Paris.
technology.context: He showed it in December.

arts_culture.text: Igor Stravinsky's ballet The Firebird premieres in Paris, danced by the Ballets Russes.

politics.text: An army uprising at Wuchang, in China, begins the revolution that will overthrow the Qing dynasty.
politics.context: It began in October.

society.text: The Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and his team reach the South Pole.
society.context: They arrived in December.

technology.text: The New Zealand-born physicist Ernest Rutherford proposes that atoms have a tiny, dense nucleus at their centre.
technology.context: He announced his model in Manchester.

arts_culture.text: The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre, in Paris, by an Italian workman, Vincenzo Peruggia.
arts_culture.context: It was stolen in August and recovered two years later.

politics.text: Puyi, the last child emperor of China's Qing dynasty, abdicates after the Xinhai Revolution.
politics.context: He gave up the throne in February. China became a republic.

politics.text: African leaders meet in Bloemfontein and found the organisation that becomes the African National Congress.
politics.context: It was founded in January, as the South African Native National Congress.

society.text: The British explorer Robert Falcon Scott reaches the South Pole and finds a Norwegian flag already planted there.
society.context: He reached the Pole in January. None of his party survived the return.

technology.text: The Austrian physicist Victor Hess rides a balloon to great height and discovers cosmic rays.
technology.context: The flight was in August. He found that radiation increases with altitude.

arts_culture.text: The Spanish painter Pablo Picasso glues a piece of oilcloth onto a canvas in Paris, creating his first collage.
arts_culture.context: The work is Still Life with Chair Caning, an early landmark of Cubism.

politics.text: American forces occupy the Mexican port of Veracruz, during the Mexican Revolution.
politics.context: They landed in April.

society.text: British and German soldiers stop fighting and meet in no man's land on Christmas Day.
society.context: The truce was spontaneous and unofficial.

technology.text: The Panama Canal opens, letting ships sail between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
technology.context: The first ship passed through in August.

arts_culture.text: Charlie Chaplin first appears as the Tramp, in a short film made in Venice, California.
arts_culture.context: The film was released in February.

politics.text: The British government issues the Balfour Declaration, supporting a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
politics.context: It was issued in November.

society.text: A ship loaded with explosives blows up in Halifax harbour, in Canada, in the largest man-made explosion of its time.
society.context: It happened in December.

technology.text: British tanks attack in large numbers for the first time at the Battle of Cambrai, in France.
technology.context: The battle began in November.

arts_culture.text: The French artist Marcel Duchamp submits a porcelain urinal signed "R. Mutt", titled Fountain, to an exhibition in New York.

politics.text: British troops open fire on an unarmed crowd at the Jallianwala Bagh, in Amritsar, India.
politics.context: The massacre took place in April.

politics.text: The Allies and Germany sign the Treaty of Versailles in the Hall of Mirrors, formally ending the First World War with Germany.
politics.context: It was signed in June.

society.text: A giant tank of molasses bursts in Boston, Massachusetts, sending a sticky wave through the streets.
society.context: It burst in January.

technology.text: Astronomers led by Arthur Eddington photograph a solar eclipse from the island of Príncipe, off West Africa, to test Einstein's theory.
technology.context: The May observations supported Einstein's predictions.

arts_culture.text: The German architect Walter Gropius founds the Bauhaus school of art and design in Weimar.

politics.text: The League of Nations holds its first council meeting, in Paris.
politics.context: It met in January.

society.text: Prohibition begins in the United States, banning the making and selling of alcoholic drinks.
society.context: It took effect in January.

technology.text: Station KDKA in Pittsburgh makes the first scheduled commercial radio broadcast, reporting the results of a presidential election.
technology.context: It broadcast in November.

arts_culture.text: The German film The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari premieres in Berlin and sets the style of expressionist cinema.

politics.text: Benito Mussolini's Blackshirts march on Rome, and the king of Italy invites him to form a government.
politics.context: The march took place in October.

politics.text: The Ottoman sultanate is abolished, ending the rule of a dynasty that lasted more than six centuries.
politics.context: The sultanate was abolished in November.

society.text: The English archaeologist Howard Carter finds the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings, in Egypt.
society.context: He found the first steps in November and entered the burial chamber later.

technology.text: Canadian doctors in Toronto give insulin to a boy dying of diabetes, the first patient treated with it.
technology.context: The patient was Leonard Thompson, aged fourteen, in January. Frederick Banting led the work.

arts_culture.text: The Irish writer James Joyce's novel Ulysses is published in Paris, on his fortieth birthday.
arts_culture.context: It was published in February by Sylvia Beach.

politics.text: Mustafa Kemal, later called Atatürk, proclaims the Republic of Turkey.
politics.context: He proclaimed it in October.

politics.text: Adolf Hitler and his Nazis attempt to seize power in a failed coup in a Munich beer hall.
politics.context: The Beer Hall Putsch was in November.

society.text: A huge earthquake strikes Tokyo and Yokohama, in Japan, and fires destroy much of both cities.
society.context: The Great Kantō earthquake struck on the first of September.

technology.text: The Russian-born engineer Vladimir Zworykin applies for a patent for the iconoscope, an early television camera tube.
technology.context: He applied in December.

arts_culture.text: The brothers Walt and Roy Disney found a small cartoon studio in Hollywood, California.
arts_culture.context: It was set up in October.

politics.text: Vladimir Lenin, the founder of the Soviet state, dies near Moscow.
politics.context: He died in January.

society.text: The first Winter Olympic Games are held in Chamonix, in the French Alps.
society.context: They opened in January.

technology.text: Two American Army aircraft complete the first flight around the world, after nearly six months.
technology.context: They finished in September.

arts_culture.text: George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue premieres at a concert in New York, with the composer at the piano.

politics.text: Hirohito becomes emperor of Japan, beginning the Shōwa era.
politics.context: He took the throne on Christmas Day.

society.text: A general strike by British trade unions in support of coal miners brings the United Kingdom to a halt.
society.context: The General Strike lasted nine days in May.

technology.text: The American physicist Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fuelled rocket in Massachusetts.
technology.context: It was launched in March.

technology.text: The Scottish inventor John Logie Baird demonstrates a working television system in London.
technology.context: He gave the demonstration in January.

arts_culture.text: The English author A. A. Milne publishes Winnie-the-Pooh, with drawings by E. H. Shepard.

politics.text: Chiang Kai-shek's forces turn on their Communist allies in Shanghai, in a bloody purge.
politics.context: It happened in April.

society.text: The American pilot Charles Lindbergh flies solo and non-stop from New York to Paris.
society.context: He landed in May.

technology.text: The young American inventor Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first fully electronic television system, in San Francisco.
technology.context: The first image was transmitted in September.

arts_culture.text: Fritz Lang's science-fiction film Metropolis premieres in Berlin.

politics.text: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist forces take the old imperial capital, Beijing, and nominally reunify China.
politics.context: The Northern Expedition captured the city in June.

society.text: British women win the vote on the same terms as men, when Parliament passes the Equal Franchise Act.
society.context: The voting age for women was lowered to 21.

technology.text: The Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming notices a mould killing bacteria on a forgotten dish in London, and discovers penicillin.
technology.context: The discovery was in September.

arts_culture.text: Walt Disney's cartoon mouse, Mickey, whistles his way through the short film Steamboat Willie in New York.
arts_culture.context: It premiered in November, with synchronised sound.

arts_culture.text: The German playwright Bertolt Brecht and the composer Kurt Weill's The Threepenny Opera premieres in Berlin.
arts_culture.context: It opened in August and includes the song Mack the Knife.

politics.text: The Lateran Treaty is signed, creating the Vatican City as an independent state inside Rome.
politics.context: It was signed in February by Mussolini's government and the Pope.

society.text: The New York stock market crashes, and a long worldwide depression begins.
society.context: The crash came in late October.

technology.text: The airship Graf Zeppelin flies around the world, carrying passengers.
technology.context: The flight took place in August.

arts_culture.text: The Belgian cartoonist Hergé creates Tintin, the boy reporter, for a children's newspaper supplement.
arts_culture.context: The first story began in January.

politics.text: Mahatma Gandhi leads the Salt March to the sea at Dandi, to protest against the British salt tax.
politics.context: It began in March.

society.text: Uruguay hosts and wins the first football World Cup, in Montevideo.
society.context: The final was in July.

technology.text: The American astronomer Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto, at the Lowell Observatory in Arizona.
technology.context: The discovery was announced in March.

arts_culture.text: The American painter Grant Wood paints American Gothic, a stern farmer and his daughter in front of a house.
arts_culture.context: It was exhibited in Chicago in the autumn.

politics.text: Abdulaziz ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, uniting his territories under one name.
politics.context: The kingdom was proclaimed in September.

society.text: The American aviator Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.
society.context: She flew in May, from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland.

society.text: The Sydney Harbour Bridge opens, linking the north and south shores of the Australian city.
society.context: It opened in March.

technology.text: The English physicist James Chadwick discovers the neutron at the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge.
technology.context: He announced it in February.

arts_culture.text: The English writer Aldous Huxley publishes Brave New World, a novel about a future society controlled by pleasure.
arts_culture.context: It came out in the winter.

politics.text: Italian forces under Marshal Pietro Badoglio enter Addis Ababa and capture Ethiopia's capital.
politics.context: They entered in May. Emperor Haile Selassie went into exile.

politics.text: General Francisco Franco leads a military uprising against Spain's elected government, beginning the Spanish Civil War.
politics.context: The uprising began in July.

society.text: The American athlete Jesse Owens wins four gold medals at the Berlin Olympic Games, in front of Adolf Hitler.
society.context: The Games took place in August.

technology.text: The British mathematician Alan Turing publishes his paper on computable numbers, describing an imaginary machine that can compute anything.
technology.context: His paper laid the foundation for computer science.

technology.text: The BBC begins the world's first regular public high-definition television service, from Alexandra Palace in London.
technology.context: The service started in November.

arts_culture.text: Charlie Chaplin's film Modern Times, about a factory worker and the machine age, is released in the United States.

politics.text: Japanese and Chinese troops clash at the Marco Polo Bridge, near Beijing, starting a full-scale war.
politics.context: It happened in July.

society.text: The German airship Hindenburg bursts into flames as it lands in New Jersey.
society.context: It happened in May.

technology.text: The British engineer Frank Whittle runs the first jet engine on a test bed in Rugby, England.
technology.context: The test was in April.

arts_culture.text: Pablo Picasso paints Guernica, a huge black-and-white protest against the bombing of a Basque town.
arts_culture.context: He painted it in Paris in the spring.

politics.text: Mexican president Lázaro Cárdenas nationalises the country's oil industry, taking it from foreign companies.
politics.context: He announced it in March.

society.text: Nazi mobs attack Jewish homes, shops and synagogues across Germany and Austria in the Kristallnacht pogrom.
society.context: It took place on the night of the ninth to the tenth of November.

technology.text: German chemists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann split the uranium atom in Berlin, discovering nuclear fission.
technology.context: The experiment was in December. Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explained it.

arts_culture.text: Orson Welles's radio drama of The War of the Worlds convinces some American listeners that Martians are invading.
arts_culture.context: It was broadcast in October, on the eve of Halloween.

arts_culture.text: Superman, created by two young Americans, Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster, first appears on the cover of Action Comics.
arts_culture.context: The comic went on sale in the spring.

politics.text: The Philippines becomes independent from the United States, after nearly half a century of American rule.
politics.context: Independence came on the fourth of July.

society.text: Judges at Nuremberg, in Germany, deliver verdicts on leading Nazis, sentencing twelve to death.
society.context: The verdicts came in October.

technology.text: The first general-purpose electronic computer, ENIAC, is unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania.
technology.context: It was unveiled in February.

arts_culture.text: The French writer and director Jean Cocteau releases his film Beauty and the Beast, based on the fairy tale.
arts_culture.context: It was released in the autumn.

politics.text: Britain divides India into two independent countries, India and Pakistan, in a partition that displaces millions.
politics.context: The partition took place in August.

society.text: Jackie Robinson plays his first game for the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking baseball's colour bar.
society.context: It was in April.

technology.text: Researchers at Bell Laboratories in New Jersey demonstrate the first working transistor.
technology.context: The demonstration was in December. Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley shared a Nobel Prize for it.

technology.text: The American pilot Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier in a rocket plane over California.
technology.context: The flight was in October.

arts_culture.text: A young Dutch girl's diary, written while hiding from the Nazis in Amsterdam, is first published.
arts_culture.context: Anne Frank's Het Achterhuis appeared in June, edited by her father Otto.

arts_culture.text: The first Edinburgh International Festival is held in Scotland, bringing theatre and music to a war-weary Britain.

politics.text: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel in Tel Aviv, and neighbouring Arab states invade.
politics.context: It was proclaimed in May.

society.text: The Indian leader Mahatma Gandhi is shot dead in New Delhi by a Hindu nationalist, Nathuram Godse.
society.context: He was killed on the last day of January.

technology.text: Columbia Records in New York introduces the long-playing vinyl record, which holds about twenty minutes per side.
technology.context: It was introduced in June.

arts_culture.text: The Italian director Vittorio De Sica releases Bicycle Thieves, a neorealist film about a poor Roman whose bicycle is stolen.

politics.text: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing.
politics.context: He proclaimed it on the first of October.

politics.text: Twelve countries sign the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, creating the NATO alliance.
politics.context: It was signed in April.

society.text: South Africa passes a law banning marriages between white and non-white people, early in its apartheid programme.
society.context: The Prohibition of Mixed Marriages Act passed in the summer.

technology.text: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb at a site in Kazakhstan.
technology.context: The test was in August, sooner than Western experts had expected.

arts_culture.text: The English writer George Orwell publishes his novel of a totalitarian future, in which Big Brother watches everyone.

politics.text: North Korean forces cross the border into South Korea, beginning the Korean War.
politics.context: The invasion began in late June.

politics.text: India becomes a republic and adopts its constitution, with Rajendra Prasad as its first president.
politics.context: It came into force on the twenty-sixth of January.

society.text: Diners Club issues the first general-purpose charge card in New York, starting the credit card age.
society.context: It was issued in February.
