technology.text: The British mathematician Alan Turing publishes a paper asking whether machines can think, and proposes an imitation game.
technology.context: It appeared in the journal Mind in October. The game is now called the Turing test.

arts_culture.text: The American cartoonist Charles Schulz launches the comic strip Peanuts, featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy.

politics.text: Army officers overthrow King Farouk of Egypt in a coup led by the Free Officers.
politics.context: The coup was in July.

society.text: A thick smog settles over London and kills thousands of people, in the Great Smog.
society.context: It lasted for several days in December.

technology.text: The United States tests the first hydrogen bomb, at Enewetak Atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
technology.context: The test was in November.

arts_culture.text: The American writer Ernest Hemingway publishes The Old Man and the Sea.

politics.text: Iran's prime minister, Mohammad Mosaddegh, is overthrown in a coup backed by American and British intelligence agencies.
politics.context: He was removed in August. The Shah returned to power.

politics.text: The Soviet leader Joseph Stalin dies at his dacha near Moscow, after almost three decades in power.
politics.context: He died in March.

society.text: The New Zealand beekeeper Edmund Hillary and the Sherpa climber Tenzing Norgay reach the summit of Mount Everest.
society.context: They reached the top in May, as part of a British expedition.

society.text: The young Queen Elizabeth II is crowned in Westminster Abbey, in a ceremony broadcast on television to millions.
society.context: The coronation was in June.

technology.text: James Watson and Francis Crick, two researchers at Cambridge, describe the double-helix structure of DNA.
technology.context: The paper was published in April.

arts_culture.text: Samuel Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, in which two men wait for someone who never arrives, premieres in a small Paris theatre.

politics.text: Vietnamese forces under General Võ Nguyên Giáp defeat the French at Dien Bien Phu.
politics.context: The battle ended in May.

society.text: The British runner Roger Bannister runs the first mile in under four minutes, at Oxford.
society.context: He did it in May.

technology.text: The United States launches Nautilus, the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.
technology.context: It was launched in January.

arts_culture.text: The Japanese film Godzilla, about a giant monster awakened by nuclear tests, premieres in Tokyo.

politics.text: Leaders of twenty-nine Asian and African countries meet at Bandung, in Indonesia, to oppose colonialism.
politics.context: The conference was in April.

society.text: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, and is arrested, sparking a bus boycott.
society.context: It happened on the first of December.

society.text: Disneyland opens in Anaheim, California.
society.context: It opened in July.

technology.text: The American researcher Jonas Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective.
technology.context: The announcement came in April.

arts_culture.text: The Indian director Satyajit Ray releases his first film, Pather Panchali, about a poor family in rural Bengal.

politics.text: Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt after President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal.
politics.context: The attack came in October. Under heavy pressure, the three countries withdrew.

politics.text: Soviet tanks crush the Hungarian uprising in Budapest.
politics.context: The revolution began in October and was put down in early November.

society.text: Melbourne becomes the first city in the southern hemisphere to host the Summer Olympic Games.
society.context: They opened in November.

technology.text: IBM, in California, introduces the first commercial computer with a hard disk drive, the RAMAC.
technology.context: It was announced in September.

arts_culture.text: The young American singer Elvis Presley releases his first album and is soon a national sensation.
arts_culture.context: The album came out in March, after the single Heartbreak Hotel.

politics.text: Ghana becomes the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence from Britain, under Kwame Nkrumah.
politics.context: Independence came in March.

politics.text: Six European countries sign the Treaty of Rome, founding the European Economic Community.
politics.context: It was signed in March, in the Italian capital.

society.text: Nine Black students, escorted by federal troops, enter Central High School in Little Rock, Arkansas.
society.context: They entered in September, on the order of President Eisenhower.

technology.text: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik, the first artificial satellite, from Baikonur in Kazakhstan.
technology.context: It was launched in October and started the space race.

arts_culture.text: Jack Kerouac publishes On the Road, a novel about restless friends driving across America, which he typed on one long scroll.
Leonard Bernstein's musical West Side Story, a modern retelling of Romeo and Juliet, opens on Broadway.

politics.text: Mao Zedong launches the Great Leap Forward, an attempt to industrialise China very fast.
politics.context: It began in the early part of the year.

society.text: The Brussels World's Fair opens with the Atomium, a giant model of an iron crystal.
society.context: It opened in April.

technology.text: The American engineer Jack Kilby demonstrates the first working integrated circuit at Texas Instruments.
technology.context: He demonstrated it in September.

arts_culture.text: The Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe publishes Things Fall Apart.

politics.text: Fidel Castro's rebels take Havana as the dictator Fulgencio Batista flees Cuba.
politics.context: Batista left at the very start of the year.

society.text: The Dalai Lama flees Tibet for India after a failed uprising against Chinese rule in Lhasa.
society.context: He escaped in March.

technology.text: A Soviet space probe crashes into the Moon on purpose, the first human-made object to reach another world.
technology.context: The probe was Luna 2, in September.

arts_culture.text: The American trumpeter Miles Davis records Kind of Blue, one of the best-selling jazz albums of all time.

politics.text: The Belgian Congo becomes independent, with Patrice Lumumba as its first prime minister.
politics.context: Independence was declared on the last day of June.

politics.text: John F. Kennedy narrowly wins the American presidential election, defeating Richard Nixon.
politics.context: The vote was in November.

society.text: The most powerful earthquake ever recorded strikes southern Chile, near the city of Valdivia.
society.context: It struck in May.

technology.text: The American physicist Theodore Maiman operates the first working laser, in California.
technology.context: He did it in May.

arts_culture.text: Alfred Hitchcock's thriller Psycho, with its famous shower scene, is released.

politics.text: Cuban exiles trained by the CIA land at the Bay of Pigs and are crushed by Fidel Castro's forces.
politics.context: The invasion took place in April.

politics.text: East German authorities begin building the Berlin Wall, dividing the city.
politics.context: The barrier went up overnight in August.

society.text: The trial of Adolf Eichmann, a chief organiser of the Holocaust, opens in Jerusalem.
society.context: It opened in April.

society.text: Black and white activists ride buses through the American South to challenge segregation, as the Freedom Riders.
society.context: The first rides left Washington in May.

technology.text: The Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin becomes the first person in space, orbiting the Earth once in Vostok.
technology.context: The flight took place in April and lasted under two hours.

arts_culture.text: Audrey Hepburn stars as Holly Golightly in the film Breakfast at Tiffany's, based on a novella by Truman Capote.

politics.text: Algeria becomes independent from France after a bitter war of independence.
politics.context: Independence came on the third of July.

society.text: The American biologist Rachel Carson publishes Silent Spring, a warning about pesticides that inspires the environmental movement.
society.context: It came out in September.

technology.text: The communications satellite Telstar is launched, and sends the first live television pictures across the Atlantic.
technology.context: It was launched in July.

arts_culture.text: The first James Bond film, Dr. No, premieres in London, starring Sean Connery.

politics.text: Nelson Mandela is sentenced to life in prison at the end of the Rivonia Trial in South Africa.
politics.context: The sentence came in June.

politics.text: President Lyndon Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act, outlawing segregation and discrimination in the United States.
politics.context: He signed it in July.

society.text: Tokyo hosts the Summer Olympic Games, the first held in Asia.
society.context: They opened in October.

technology.text: Japan opens the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, a high-speed railway running between Tokyo and Osaka at record speed.
technology.context: It opened in October, just before the Olympics.

arts_culture.text: The British band the Beatles appear on The Ed Sullivan Show in New York and set off a wave of hysteria in America.

politics.text: Singapore leaves the Federation of Malaysia and becomes an independent republic under Lee Kuan Yew.
politics.context: It separated in August.

society.text: Civil rights marchers are beaten by state troopers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, on Bloody Sunday.
society.context: It happened in March.

technology.text: The Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk, floating outside his spacecraft for about twelve minutes.
technology.context: He did it in March.

arts_culture.text: Bob Dylan plugs in an electric guitar at the Newport Folk Festival, and is booed by part of the crowd.

politics.text: Mao Zedong launches the Cultural Revolution in China, mobilising young Red Guards against his rivals.
politics.context: It began in May.

society.text: England's footballers beat West Germany at Wembley Stadium to win the World Cup.
society.context: The final was in July and went to extra time.

technology.text: A Soviet space probe makes the first soft landing on the Moon and sends back photographs from the surface.
technology.context: The probe was Luna 9. It landed in February.

arts_culture.text: The British band the Beatles release Revolver, an album that pushes pop music into studio experiments.

politics.text: Israel defeats Egypt, Jordan and Syria in the Six-Day War, capturing the Sinai, the West Bank and the Golan Heights.
politics.context: The war was fought in June.

society.text: Tens of thousands of young people gather in San Francisco for the "Summer of Love", centred on the Haight-Ashbury district.
society.context: It took place over the summer.

technology.text: The South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performs the world's first human heart transplant in Cape Town.
technology.context: He operated in December. The patient lived for eighteen days.

arts_culture.text: The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, which many critics call one of the greatest albums ever.

politics.text: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces launch the Tet Offensive across South Vietnam, shocking American public opinion.
politics.context: It began in late January.

politics.text: Soviet-led Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia to crush the reforms of the Prague Spring.
politics.context: The invasion was in August.

society.text: Student protests and a general strike shake France, almost bringing down President Charles de Gaulle's government.
society.context: The unrest peaked in May.

society.text: The civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee.
society.context: He was shot in April.

technology.text: The American astronauts on the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon read from the Book of Genesis on Christmas Eve.
technology.context: The mission was Apollo 8, in December.

arts_culture.text: Stanley Kubrick's science-fiction film about a black monolith and the computer HAL premieres.

politics.text: Golda Meir becomes Prime Minister of Israel.
politics.context: She took office in March.

society.text: The Woodstock festival draws about four hundred thousand people to a farm in upstate New York.
society.context: It was held in August.

technology.text: The first message is sent over ARPANET, the computer network that grew into the internet.
technology.context: It was sent between computers at UCLA and Stanford in October.

arts_culture.text: The Beatles release Abbey Road, whose cover shows them crossing a London street.

politics.text: East Pakistan wins independence from Pakistan, with Indian help, after a bloody war, and becomes Bangladesh.
politics.context: The Liberation War ended in December.

society.text: Swiss men vote in a national referendum to give women the right to vote in federal elections.
society.context: The referendum was held in February.

technology.text: The American company Intel releases the first microprocessor, a fingernail-sized chip holding a whole computer processor.
technology.context: The chip was the 4004. It was released in November.

technology.text: The American programmer Ray Tomlinson sends the first email between two computers on a network, in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
technology.context: He also chose the @ sign to separate the user's name from the computer's.

arts_culture.text: The former Beatle John Lennon releases Imagine, an album whose title song pictures a world without possessions or borders.

politics.text: American president Richard Nixon visits Beijing and meets Mao Zedong, opening relations with China.
politics.context: It happened in February.

society.text: Palestinian gunmen take Israeli athletes hostage at the Munich Olympic Games, and eleven of them are killed.
society.context: The Munich massacre took place in September.

technology.text: Atari releases Pong, one of the first successful video games, in an arcade in California.
technology.context: It was released in November.

arts_culture.text: Francis Ford Coppola's film The Godfather, based on Mario Puzo's novel about a Mafia family, is released.

politics.text: General Augusto Pinochet's army seizes power in Chile, and President Salvador Allende dies in the presidential palace.
politics.context: The coup took place in September.

politics.text: Egypt and Syria launch a surprise attack on Israel on the holy day of Yom Kippur.
politics.context: The war began in October.

society.text: Arab oil producers cut supplies to countries that backed Israel in the Yom Kippur War, causing fuel queues and price shocks.
society.context: The oil embargo began in October.

technology.text: The Motorola engineer Martin Cooper makes the first handheld mobile phone call, on a street in New York.
technology.context: It was in April. He rang a rival at Bell Labs.

arts_culture.text: Queen Elizabeth II opens the Sydney Opera House, with sail-like roofs designed by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon.
arts_culture.context: It opened in October. Utzon had left the project years earlier and did not attend.

politics.text: Army officers overthrow the dictatorship in Lisbon, and people put carnations in soldiers' rifles.
politics.context: The Carnation Revolution happened on the twenty-fifth of April.

society.text: Muhammad Ali beats George Foreman in the "Rumble in the Jungle", in Kinshasa, in Zaire.
society.context: The fight was in October.

technology.text: American and French researchers find the skeleton of an early human relative, nicknamed Lucy, in Ethiopia.
technology.context: The find was in November. She was named after a Beatles song.

arts_culture.text: The Swedish pop group ABBA wins the Eurovision Song Contest with "Waterloo", in Brighton, England.

politics.text: North Vietnamese tanks enter Saigon, ending the Vietnam War, and South Vietnam's government surrenders.
politics.context: It happened on the last day of April.

politics.text: The Khmer Rouge enter Phnom Penh, beginning Pol Pot's brutal rule over Cambodia.
politics.context: They entered the capital in April.

society.text: Muhammad Ali beats Joe Frazier in the "Thrilla in Manila", one of the greatest fights in boxing history.
society.context: It was held in October. Frazier's corner stopped the fight.

technology.text: Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft in Albuquerque, New Mexico, to write software for the Altair personal computer.
technology.context: They founded it in April.

arts_culture.text: Steven Spielberg's film Jaws, about a shark terrorising a New England beach town, opens and becomes the first summer blockbuster.

politics.text: Schoolchildren protest against Afrikaans-language teaching in Soweto, and police open fire, igniting a nationwide uprising.
politics.context: The Soweto uprising began on the sixteenth of June.

society.text: The Romanian gymnast Nadia Comăneci scores the first perfect mark in Olympic gymnastics, at the Montreal Games.
society.context: The Games were in July. The scoreboard showed 1.00, as it could not display a ten.

technology.text: Britain and France begin the first supersonic passenger flights with Concorde.
technology.context: Services began in January.

technology.text: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak found Apple Computer, in a garage in California.
technology.context: They founded it in April.

arts_culture.text: The British punk band the Sex Pistols swear on live television in London, causing a national scandal.
arts_culture.context: The interview was broadcast in December.

politics.text: Egyptian president Anwar Sadat visits Jerusalem, the first Arab leader to go to Israel.
politics.context: He went in November.

society.text: A huge power cut plunges New York City into darkness, followed by looting and fires.
society.context: The blackout was in July.

technology.text: NASA launches two Voyager probes on a grand tour of the outer planets.
technology.context: They were launched in August and September.

arts_culture.text: George Lucas's space adventure Star Wars opens in American cinemas.

politics.text: The Shah of Iran flees, and the Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile in Paris to replace the monarchy with an Islamic republic.
politics.context: The revolution succeeded in February.

politics.text: Soviet troops invade Afghanistan to prop up its communist government.
politics.context: The invasion began in late December.

society.text: A reactor at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania partly melts down, changing America's nuclear debate for good.
society.context: The accident happened in March.

technology.text: The Japanese company Sony launches the Walkman, a portable cassette player, in Tokyo.
technology.context: It went on sale in July.

arts_culture.text: Francis Ford Coppola's Vietnam war film Apocalypse Now, based on a novella by Joseph Conrad, shares the top prize at Cannes.

politics.text: Iraq invades Iran, starting a war that lasts eight years.
politics.context: It began in September.

politics.text: Lech Wałęsa leads striking shipyard workers in Gdańsk to found Solidarity, the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc.
politics.context: It was founded in August.

society.text: A volcano erupts in the state of Washington, killing dozens and blasting the top off the mountain.
society.context: Mount St. Helens erupted in May.

society.text: The former Beatle John Lennon is shot dead outside his home in New York City.
society.context: He was killed in December.

technology.text: The World Health Organization declares that smallpox has been wiped out from the world.
technology.context: The declaration was made in May.

arts_culture.text: The Italian writer Umberto Eco publishes his medieval murder mystery The Name of the Rose.

politics.text: Egyptian president Anwar Sadat is assassinated by soldiers during a military parade in Cairo.
politics.context: He was killed in October.

society.text: Prince Charles marries Lady Diana Spencer at Saint Paul's Cathedral, in front of a worldwide television audience.
society.context: The wedding was in July.

technology.text: IBM launches its Personal Computer, setting the standard for desktop computers.
technology.context: It was launched in August.

arts_culture.text: The music channel MTV launches in the United States, opening with the video for Video Killed the Radio Star.

politics.text: Israel invades Lebanon, aiming to destroy Palestinian forces, and reaches the outskirts of Beirut.
politics.context: It began in June.

politics.text: Argentine forces seize the Falkland Islands, and Britain sends a naval task force to retake them.
politics.context: The invasion was in April.

society.text: The warship Mary Rose, pride of King Henry VIII's navy, is lifted from the seabed off Portsmouth after centuries underwater.
society.context: It was raised in October.

technology.text: Sony and Philips launch the compact disc, with the first CD players going on sale in Japan.
technology.context: They launched in October.

arts_culture.text: Michael Jackson releases Thriller, which becomes the best-selling album of all time.

politics.text: The Indian prime minister Indira Gandhi is assassinated by two of her Sikh bodyguards in New Delhi.
politics.context: It happened in October.

society.text: A gas leak at a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, kills thousands in one of the worst industrial disasters ever.
society.context: It happened in December.

technology.text: Apple launches the Macintosh, a personal computer with a mouse and a graphical screen, after a famous Super Bowl advert.
technology.context: It was launched in January.

arts_culture.text: British and Irish pop stars, led by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure, record Do They Know It's Christmas? for Ethiopian famine relief.
arts_culture.context: The group was called Band Aid. The song was recorded in November and released in December.

politics.text: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes leader of the Soviet Union and begins a programme of reform.
politics.context: He took power in March.

society.text: Rock stars play the Live Aid concerts in London and Philadelphia to raise money for famine victims in Ethiopia.
society.context: The concerts were in July.

technology.text: A team led by Robert Ballard finds the wreck of the Titanic on the floor of the North Atlantic.
technology.context: They found it in September.

arts_culture.text: The film Back to the Future, in which a teenager travels through time in a car, opens in American cinemas.

politics.text: Millions of Filipinos take to the streets of Manila in the People Power Revolution, ending Ferdinand Marcos's rule.
politics.context: It took place in February.

society.text: A reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine, spreading radioactive fallout across Europe.
society.context: It exploded in April.

society.text: The American space shuttle Challenger breaks apart shortly after launch, killing all seven crew members.
society.context: It happened in January.

technology.text: The Soviet Union launches the core module of the Mir space station.
technology.context: It was launched in February.

arts_culture.text: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical The Phantom of the Opera opens in London, starring Michael Crawford and Sarah Brightman.

politics.text: Chinese troops crush student-led demonstrations in Tiananmen Square in Beijing.
politics.context: The protests were crushed in June.

society.text: The tanker Exxon Valdez runs aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, and spills millions of gallons of crude oil.
society.context: The spill happened in March.

society.text: Ninety-seven Liverpool supporters die in a crush at Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield, England.
society.context: It happened in April. The toll was first given as ninety-six.

technology.text: Tim Berners-Lee, a British researcher at CERN in Switzerland, proposes a system for sharing documents through linked pages.
technology.context: He wrote the proposal for the World Wide Web in March.

arts_culture.text: Iran's Ayatollah Khomeini calls for the death of the British novelist Salman Rushdie over his book The Satanic Verses.
arts_culture.context: The fatwa was issued in February.

politics.text: Iraq invades Kuwait under Saddam Hussein, setting off a crisis that leads to the Gulf War.
politics.context: The invasion was in August.

politics.text: East and West Germany reunite as one country.
politics.context: Reunification took place on the third of October.

society.text: The first McDonald's restaurant in the Soviet Union opens in Pushkin Square, in Moscow, with huge queues.
society.context: It opened in January.

technology.text: NASA launches the Hubble Space Telescope aboard the space shuttle Discovery.
technology.context: It was launched in April. Its mirror proved flawed and was repaired three years later.

arts_culture.text: David Lynch's television series Twin Peaks, about the murder of a teenage girl in a small town, begins on American television.

politics.text: The Soviet Union is dissolved after Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as its president.
politics.context: He resigned on Christmas Day.

politics.text: A coalition led by the United States begins air strikes on Iraq, opening the Gulf War to free Kuwait.
politics.context: The air campaign began in January.

society.text: Los Angeles police officers beat the motorist Rodney King, and a bystander films it.
society.context: It happened in March.

technology.text: A Finnish student, Linus Torvalds, announces a free operating system kernel that becomes known as Linux.
technology.context: He announced it in August.

arts_culture.text: The American band Nirvana releases Nevermind, bringing grunge to a mass audience.

politics.text: Twelve European countries sign the Maastricht Treaty, creating the European Union.
politics.context: They signed in February.

society.text: Barcelona hosts the Summer Olympic Games.
society.context: They opened in July.

technology.text: A British engineer, Neil Papworth, sends the first text message, "Merry Christmas", to a mobile phone.
technology.context: The message was sent in December.

arts_culture.text: Disney's animated film Aladdin, with a genie voiced by Robin Williams, is released.

politics.text: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization sign the Oslo Accords on the White House lawn.
politics.context: The signing was in September.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes the state of Maharashtra, in western India, killing thousands.
society.context: The Latur earthquake struck in September.

technology.text: Students at the University of Illinois release Mosaic, a web browser that brings pictures to the internet.
technology.context: It was released in April.

arts_culture.text: Steven Spielberg's film Jurassic Park, with dinosaurs made from computer graphics, is released.

politics.text: Nelson Mandela is sworn in as South Africa's first Black president after the country's first all-race elections.
politics.context: He took office in May.

society.text: Hutu extremists begin a genocide in Rwanda, killing hundreds of thousands of Tutsi in about a hundred days.
society.context: It began in April.

technology.text: Queen Elizabeth II and French president François Mitterrand open the Channel Tunnel, linking Britain and France by rail.
technology.context: It opened in May.

technology.text: Netscape releases Navigator, a web browser that brings the internet to millions of ordinary people.
technology.context: The full version came out in December.

arts_culture.text: Quentin Tarantino's film Pulp Fiction wins the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

politics.text: Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin is assassinated by an extremist after a peace rally in Tel Aviv.
politics.context: It happened in November.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes the Japanese city of Kobe, killing thousands.
society.context: It struck in January.

technology.text: Jeff Bezos launches Amazon, selling books online, from a garage in Seattle.
technology.context: It opened to the public in July.

arts_culture.text: Pixar's film Toy Story, the first feature made entirely with computer animation, is released.

politics.text: The Taliban capture Kabul and take control of most of Afghanistan.
politics.context: They took the city in September.

society.text: A bomb explodes in a park during the Summer Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia.
society.context: It exploded in July.

technology.text: NASA launches the Mars Pathfinder mission, which will land a small rover called Sojourner on Mars.
technology.context: It was launched in December.

arts_culture.text: The film Trainspotting, about young heroin users in Edinburgh, is released in Britain.

politics.text: Britain hands Hong Kong back to Chinese rule at midnight, ending more than a century of colonial control.
politics.context: The handover took place on the first of July.

society.text: Thailand lets its currency, the baht, float, setting off a financial crisis across Asia.
society.context: The Asian financial crisis began in July.

society.text: Diana, Princess of Wales, dies in a car crash in a Paris road tunnel, and Britain goes into mass mourning.
society.context: She died on the last day of August.

technology.text: IBM's computer Deep Blue defeats the reigning world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, in a six-game match in New York.
technology.context: The match ended in May.

technology.text: Scientists at the Roslin Institute, in Scotland, announce Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
technology.context: The announcement was in February. Dolly was born the previous July.

arts_culture.text: The British author J. K. Rowling publishes Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, a book about a boy wizard, in a small first print run.
arts_culture.context: It came out in June, from the publisher Bloomsbury.

politics.text: Political parties in Northern Ireland sign the Good Friday Agreement, ending decades of conflict known as the Troubles.
politics.context: It was signed in April.

society.text: Hurricane Mitch hits Central America, killing thousands in Honduras and Nicaragua.
society.context: It struck in October.

technology.text: Two Stanford students, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, found the search company Google in California.
technology.context: They founded it in September.

arts_culture.text: James Cameron's film Titanic wins eleven Academy Awards, equalling the record.
arts_culture.context: The Oscars ceremony was in March.

politics.text: American and British forces begin air strikes on Afghanistan, after the attacks of the previous month.
politics.context: The strikes began in October.

society.text: The energy company Enron files for bankruptcy, the largest in American history at the time.
society.context: It filed in December.

technology.text: Apple releases the iPod, a pocket-sized digital music player.
technology.context: It was released in October.

arts_culture.text: The French romantic comedy Amélie, set in Paris, is released and becomes a hit around the world.

politics.text: An American-led coalition invades Iraq and topples Saddam Hussein.
politics.context: The invasion began in March.

society.text: The American space shuttle Columbia breaks apart on re-entry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts.
society.context: It happened on the first of February.

technology.text: Scientists announce that the Human Genome Project has finished mapping the human genome.
technology.context: The announcement was in April, fifty years after the discovery of DNA's structure.

arts_culture.text: Peter Jackson's film The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King premieres in Wellington, New Zealand.
arts_culture.context: The premiere was in December. The film later won eleven Oscars.

politics.text: The Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat dies in a military hospital near Paris.
politics.context: He died in November.

politics.text: Viktor Yushchenko wins Ukraine's presidency after mass protests overturn a rigged election, in the Orange Revolution.
politics.context: The rerun vote was in December.

society.text: A huge undersea earthquake off Sumatra triggers a tsunami that kills more than two hundred thousand people around the Indian Ocean.
society.context: It struck on the day after Christmas.

technology.text: The Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg launches Facebook from his university dormitory.
technology.context: It launched in February.

arts_culture.text: Pixar's animated film The Incredibles, about a family of superheroes in hiding, is released.

politics.text: The former Lebanese prime minister Rafic Hariri is killed by a huge car bomb in Beirut.
politics.context: The attack was in February.

society.text: A powerful earthquake strikes Kashmir, killing tens of thousands of people in Pakistan and India.
society.context: It struck in October.

society.text: Hurricane Katrina floods much of New Orleans, Louisiana, and kills more than a thousand people.
society.context: It struck at the end of August.

technology.text: Three former PayPal employees launch YouTube, a site for sharing videos, in California.
technology.context: It was founded in February.

arts_culture.text: The Taiwanese director Ang Lee's film Brokeback Mountain, about two cowboys in love, is released.

politics.text: Buddhist monks lead mass protests against the military government of Myanmar, in what is called the Saffron Revolution.
politics.context: The protests ran from August to October.

society.text: Customers queue outside Northern Rock branches in Britain, in the first run on a British bank in over a century.
society.context: The run began in September, an early sign of the financial crisis.

technology.text: Apple, led by Steve Jobs, puts the first iPhone, a touchscreen phone with no physical keyboard, on sale in the United States.
technology.context: It launched in June, five months after Jobs unveiled it.

arts_culture.text: J. K. Rowling's final Harry Potter novel, The Deathly Hallows, is released and sells millions of copies on its first day.

politics.text: Barack Obama is elected the first Black president of the United States.
politics.context: The election was in November.

society.text: A huge earthquake in Sichuan province, in China, kills about seventy thousand people.
society.context: It struck in May.

society.text: The investment bank Lehman Brothers collapses in the largest bankruptcy in American history, deepening the global financial crisis.
society.context: It filed in September.

technology.text: Scientists at CERN, near Geneva, switch on the Large Hadron Collider, the most powerful particle accelerator ever built.
technology.context: The first beams circulated in September.

arts_culture.text: Beijing opens the Summer Olympics with a vast ceremony at the Bird's Nest stadium, directed by Zhang Yimou.
arts_culture.context: The ceremony was held in August.

politics.text: Thousands of Iranians protest in Tehran after a disputed presidential election, in what becomes known as the Green Movement.
politics.context: The protests began in June.

society.text: A passenger jet makes an emergency landing on the Hudson River in New York, and everyone on board survives.
society.context: It happened in January.

technology.text: A programmer using the name Satoshi Nakamoto starts the Bitcoin network by creating its first block.
technology.context: It started in January.

arts_culture.text: James Cameron's film Avatar opens, and goes on to become the highest-earning film in history.

politics.text: A Tunisian street vendor, Mohamed Bouazizi, sets himself on fire in protest, sparking unrest that spreads across the Arab world.
politics.context: The act was in December. The unrest became known as the Arab Spring.

society.text: A huge earthquake devastates Haiti and its capital, Port-au-Prince.
society.context: It struck in January.

society.text: Thirty-three Chilean miners are rescued after more than two months trapped deep underground.
society.context: They were brought up in October, after sixty-nine days.

technology.text: Apple's Steve Jobs unveils the iPad, a tablet computer, in San Francisco.
technology.context: It was unveiled in January and went on sale in April.

arts_culture.text: Dubai opens the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world.

politics.text: Egypt's long-ruling president Hosni Mubarak resigns in Cairo after eighteen days of mass protests.
politics.context: He stepped down in February, during the Arab Spring.

politics.text: Libyan rebels capture Sirte, and Colonel Muammar Gaddafi is killed after months of civil war.
politics.context: He was killed in October.

society.text: A huge undersea earthquake off the coast of Japan triggers a tsunami and a nuclear emergency at Fukushima.
society.context: The Tōhoku earthquake struck in March.

technology.text: IBM's computer system Watson defeats two human champions on the American television quiz show Jeopardy!
technology.context: The win came in February.

technology.text: Apple unveils Siri, a voice assistant, on its new iPhone.
technology.context: It was unveiled in October.

arts_culture.text: The British singer Adele releases her second album, which tops the sales charts in many countries.
arts_culture.context: The album is titled 21. It was released in January.

politics.text: Mohamed Morsi is elected president of Egypt after the revolution that toppled Hosni Mubarak.
politics.context: He won in June, in the country's first free presidential election.

society.text: London hosts the Summer Olympic Games, with an opening ceremony directed by the film-maker Danny Boyle.
society.context: They opened in July.

technology.text: NASA's rover Curiosity lands on Mars after a daring "sky crane" descent.
technology.context: It landed in August.

technology.text: Scientists at CERN, near Geneva, announce the discovery of a particle consistent with the Higgs boson.
technology.context: They announced it in July.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean singer Psy releases "Gangnam Style", whose video becomes the first to reach a billion views.

politics.text: The Argentine cardinal Jorge Bergoglio is elected pope, taking the name Francis, the first pope from the Americas.
politics.context: He was elected in March.

society.text: A powerful typhoon, Haiyan, devastates the Philippines, killing thousands.
society.context: It struck in November.

technology.text: Scientists announce that the Voyager probe has left the Sun's bubble and entered interstellar space.
technology.context: NASA made the announcement in September.

technology.text: Edward Snowden, an American intelligence contractor, leaks documents revealing mass government surveillance.
technology.context: The first stories appeared in June.

arts_culture.text: The French electronic duo Daft Punk release Random Access Memories, an album that wins the major prizes.
arts_culture.context: It came out in May and won several Grammy awards.

politics.text: Russia annexes the Crimean peninsula from Ukraine, after troops without insignia take control.
politics.context: The annexation was in March.

society.text: A Malaysia Airlines jet disappears over the Indian Ocean with everyone on board, in one of aviation's great mysteries.
society.context: It vanished in March.

technology.text: The European probe Rosetta lands a small craft, Philae, on a comet.
technology.context: The landing was in November.

arts_culture.text: Richard Linklater's film Boyhood, shot over twelve years with the same cast, premieres.

politics.text: The Colombian government and the FARC guerrillas sign a peace deal to end more than fifty years of conflict.
politics.context: The first deal was signed in September and rejected by voters. A revised deal followed in November.

politics.text: British voters choose to leave the European Union in a referendum.
politics.context: The vote was in June.

society.text: Rio de Janeiro hosts the Summer Olympic Games, the first held in South America.
society.context: They opened in August.

technology.text: Google's AlphaGo program beats the Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul, South Korea.
technology.context: The match was in March. AlphaGo won four games to one.

arts_culture.text: The American songwriter Bob Dylan is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
arts_culture.context: The prize was announced in October.

politics.text: The leaders of North and South Korea meet at Panmunjom and sign a declaration promising peace.
politics.context: They met in April.

society.text: Twelve boys and their football coach are rescued from a flooded cave in Thailand, after more than two weeks.
society.context: The rescue was in July.

technology.text: SpaceX launches Falcon Heavy, the most powerful rocket of its day, with a sports car as a test cargo.
technology.context: It was launched in February.

arts_culture.text: Marvel's film Black Panther, set in the African kingdom of Wakanda, is released.

politics.text: The long-serving Algerian president Abdelaziz Bouteflika resigns after weeks of mass street protests.
politics.context: He resigned in April.

society.text: Fire engulfs the roof and spire of Notre-Dame cathedral in Paris.
society.context: The fire was in April.

technology.text: Astronomers with the Event Horizon Telescope release the first ever image of a black hole, in a distant galaxy.
technology.context: The image was released in April. The galaxy is Messier 87.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean director Bong Joon-ho's film Parasite wins the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
arts_culture.context: It won in May. It later won the Oscar for best picture.

politics.text: The Taliban retake Kabul as the Afghan government collapses and Western troops withdraw.
politics.context: They entered the city in August.

society.text: The container ship Ever Given runs aground in the Suez Canal and blocks it for nearly a week.
society.context: It was stuck in March.

technology.text: NASA's small helicopter Ingenuity makes the first powered flight on another planet, on Mars.
technology.context: It flew in April.

arts_culture.text: The South Korean television series Squid Game is released and becomes a global hit.

politics.text: Sri Lanka's president Gotabaya Rajapaksa flees the country as protesters storm his residence in Colombo.
politics.context: He fled in July, during an economic crisis.

politics.text: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
politics.context: The invasion began in late February.

society.text: Qatar hosts the football World Cup, and Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, beat France on penalties in the final.
society.context: The final was in December.

technology.text: The American company OpenAI releases ChatGPT, a chatbot that writes fluent text, to the public.
technology.context: It was released at the end of November.

arts_culture.text: S. S. Rajamouli's Indian film RRR, a Telugu-language action epic, is released and finds a huge global audience.

politics.text: Syria's president Bashar al-Assad flees to Russia as rebels take Damascus, ending his family's long rule.
politics.context: It happened in December.

society.text: Paris hosts the Summer Olympic Games, with an opening ceremony held along the River Seine.
society.context: The Games opened in July.

technology.text: SpaceX catches a returning Super Heavy booster with giant mechanical arms on its launch tower.
technology.context: It happened in October.

arts_culture.text: The film Wicked, based on the Broadway musical about the witches of Oz, is released.
